control-context-menu-action.summary: One entry of a [`context_menu`](/docs/control-context-menu). `content` is its label, and its own `on_click` runs when the user picks it. On Android, web, Windows and Linux the entry shows `icon` before the label and a check mark when `checked` is set; on iOS and macOS it shows `trailing_icon` after the label, in bold when `default` and in red when `destructive`. Set both icons when the menu runs everywhere.
example: status = text(value: "Right-click or long-press the file")
context_menu_action("Rename", icon: "edit", trailing_icon: "edit", on_click: ->(_event) { page.update(status, value: "Renaming report.pdf") }),
context_menu_action("Delete", icon: "delete", trailing_icon: "delete", destructive: true, on_click: ->(_event) { page.update(status, value: "Deleted report.pdf") })

control-cupertino-app-bar.summary: An iOS-style top bar. It builds the same `AppBar` control as [`app_bar`](/docs/control-app-bar), with only the keywords the iOS navigation bar uses: on iOS and macOS a `CupertinoNavigationBar` with a centered `title`, `leading` and `trailing`, and the back button label from `previous_page_title`; on Android, web, Windows and Linux a Material app bar with the same `title`, `leading` and `bgcolor`. Assign it to `page.appbar`. Ruby sends `large: false` and `transition_between_routes: true` unless you set them.
example: trailing: icon_button("edit", tooltip: "Compose", on_click: ->(_event) { page.update(status, value: "New message") }),

control-cupertino-context-menu.summary: An iOS-style context menu: a long press lifts `content` above a blurred page and shows `actions` under it. It builds the same `ContextMenu` control as [`context_menu`](/docs/control-context-menu), so on Android, web, Windows and Linux the same entries open from a right-click (a long press there needs `context_menu` with `primary_trigger: "longPress"`). Ruby sends `enable_haptic_feedback: true` unless you pass `false`. At least one action is required.
example: content: container(content: text("Beach.jpg"), width: 200, height: 120, bgcolor: "#bae6fd", padding: 16),
cupertino_context_menu_action(content: "Delete", trailing_icon: "delete", destructive: true, on_click: ->(_event) { page.update(status, value: "Deleted") })

control-cupertino-context-menu-action.summary: One entry of a [`cupertino_context_menu`](/docs/control-cupertino-context-menu). `content` is the label; on iOS and macOS `trailing_icon` shows after it, `default` draws it in bold and `destructive` in red, and picking it runs `on_click` and closes the menu. It builds the same `ContextMenuAction` control as `context_menu_action`, so on Android, web, Windows and Linux it is a plain menu entry. Ruby sends `default: false` and `destructive: false` unless you set them.
example: content: container(content: text("Shopping list"), padding: 16, bgcolor: "#fef9c3"),
cupertino_context_menu_action(content: "Pin", trailing_icon: "push_pin", default: true, on_click: ->(_event) { page.update(status, value: "Pinned") }),
cupertino_context_menu_action(content: "Delete", trailing_icon: "delete", destructive: true, on_click: ->(_event) { page.update(status, value: "Deleted") })

control-cupertino-date-picker.summary: An iOS-style wheel for picking a date, a time, or both. Open it with `page.show_dialog(picker)`: on iOS and macOS the wheel slides up with Cancel and Done, and on Android, web, Windows and Linux the client shows the Material date picker dialog. When the user confirms, `on_change` gets the picked moment in `event.data`, an ISO 8601 string in UTC. With 0.0.23 a picker added to the page shows nothing; drawing it in place with `page.add` (the wheel on iOS and macOS, a calendar elsewhere) needs the next release. **Requires the next Ruflet release** (on `main`, not in 0.0.23).

control-cupertino-dialog-action.summary: A button for the `actions` of an [`alert_dialog`](/docs/control-alert-dialog). On iOS and macOS it is the native dialog action: `default` draws it in bold, `destructive` in red, and `text_style` styles the label. It builds the same `Button` control as [`button`](/docs/control-button), so on Android, web, Windows and Linux it is a Material elevated button, and outside an alert dialog it is an iOS button without those roles. Close the dialog yourself in `on_click` with `page.pop_dialog`.

control-cupertino-filled-button.summary: An iOS-style filled button: on iOS and macOS a `CupertinoButton.filled` in the theme's primary color (or `bgcolor`). It builds the same `FilledButton` control as [`filled_button`](/docs/control-filled-button), so on Android, web, Windows and Linux it is a Material filled button, which ignores `bgcolor` and `color` because this helper has no `style:`. Known issue ([ruflet#94](https://github.com/AdamMusa/ruflet/issues/94)): with the default arguments Ruby sends an `alignment` the client cannot read, so the client draws an error box instead of the button (on iOS and macOS with 0.0.23, everywhere with `main`) and `{ "all" => 8.0 }` corners come out square. Pass `alignment: { x: 0, y: 0 }` and `border_radius: 8`, as below.

control-cupertino-navigation-bar.summary: An iOS-style bottom tab bar. It builds the same `NavigationBar` control as [`navigation_bar`](/docs/control-navigation-bar): on iOS and macOS a `CupertinoTabBar` that uses `active_color`, `inactive_color` and `icon_size`, and on Android, web, Windows and Linux a Material navigation bar. Assign it to `page.navigation_bar`; `on_change` gets the picked index in `event.data`. Ruby sends `selected_index: 0` and `icon_size: 30` unless you set them.

control-cupertino-tinted-button.summary: An iOS-style tinted button: on iOS and macOS a `CupertinoButton.tinted`, a light tint of the primary color (or of `bgcolor`) behind a colored label. It builds the same `FilledTonalButton` control as [`filled_tonal_button`](/docs/control-filled-tonal-button), so on Android, web, Windows and Linux it is a Material filled tonal button, which ignores `bgcolor` and `color` because this helper has no `style:`. Known issue ([ruflet#94](https://github.com/AdamMusa/ruflet/issues/94)): with the default arguments the client draws an error box instead of the button (on iOS and macOS with 0.0.23, everywhere with `main`) and the corners come out square. Pass `alignment: { x: 0, y: 0 }` and `border_radius: 8`, as below.

control-filled-icon-button.summary: An icon button with a solid fill, for the most important icon action on a screen. On Android, web, Windows and Linux it is a Material filled icon button; on iOS and macOS a plain iOS button with `bgcolor` behind the icon. Set `selected` for a toggle: it shows `selected_icon` and changes the fill, and you update it in `on_click`. Known issue ([ruflet#94](https://github.com/AdamMusa/ruflet/issues/94)): with the default arguments Ruby sends `alignment: "center"`, which the client cannot read, so it draws an error box instead of the button, and `{ "all" => 8 }` padding comes out as none. Pass `alignment: { x: 0, y: 0 }` and `padding: 8`, as below.

control-filled-tonal-icon-button.summary: An icon button with a soft, secondary-color fill: less emphasis than a [`filled_icon_button`](/docs/control-filled-icon-button), more than an [`icon_button`](/docs/control-icon-button). On iOS and macOS it is a plain iOS button with `bgcolor` behind the icon. Known issue ([ruflet#94](https://github.com/AdamMusa/ruflet/issues/94)): with the default arguments the client draws an error box instead of the button; pass `alignment: { x: 0, y: 0 }` and `padding: 8`, as below.

control-menu-item-button.summary: One clickable entry of a [`submenu_button`](/docs/control-submenu-button) menu in a [`menu_bar`](/docs/control-menu-bar). `content` is the label (the first positional argument), `leading` and `trailing` add controls before and after it, and `on_click` runs when the user picks it; an entry without an `on_click` handler is drawn disabled. On Android, web, Windows and Linux it is a Material menu entry; on iOS and macOS a row of the sheet the submenu opens.
example: menu_item_button("Open", leading: icon("folder_open"), on_click: ->(_event) { page.update(status, value: "Opened a file") }),
menu_item_button("Save", leading: icon("save"), on_click: ->(_event) { page.update(status, value: "Saved") })

control-navigation-bar-destination.summary: One destination of a [`navigation_bar`](/docs/control-navigation-bar) or `cupertino_navigation_bar`: an `icon` (required), a `selected_icon` shown while it is selected, and a `label` string. The bar reports the picked destination's index in `on_change`; the destination has no events of its own.

control-navigation-drawer-destination.summary: One destination of a [`navigation_drawer`](/docs/control-navigation-drawer): an `icon`, a `selected_icon` shown while it is selected, and a `label` string. The drawer reports the picked destination's index in `on_change`; the destination has no events of its own.

control-navigation-rail-destination.summary: One destination of a [`navigation_rail`](/docs/control-navigation-rail): an `icon` and a `label` (both required; the label may be a string or a control) and a `selected_icon` shown while it is selected. On Android, web, Windows and Linux `indicator_color`, `indicator_shape` and `padding` style this destination alone. The rail reports the picked destination's index in `on_change`.
example: page.add(row(expand: true, children: [rail, column(expand: true, children: [heading])]))

control-outlined-icon-button.summary: An icon button with an outline and no fill, for secondary icon actions next to a filled one. On iOS and macOS it is a plain iOS button. Known issue ([ruflet#94](https://github.com/AdamMusa/ruflet/issues/94)): with the default arguments the client draws an error box instead of the button; pass `alignment: { x: 0, y: 0 }` and `padding: 8`, as below.

control-popup-menu-item.summary: One entry in a [`popup_menu_button`](/docs/control-popup-menu-button) menu, with text, an icon, or both. Set `checked` for a check mark. The client does not change it, so keep the state yourself and update `checked` in `on_click`: `event.data` is `true` or `nil`, never `false`, and the 0.0.23 client on iOS and macOS sends none. Leave out both text and icon for a divider. Icons, check marks and dividers show on Android, web, Windows and Linux only: on iOS and macOS the menu shows each item's text and nothing else, and an item without text draws an error box.
example: popup_menu_item("Name", icon: "sort_by_alpha", on_click: ->(_event) { page.update(sort, value: "Sorted by name") }),
popup_menu_item("Date", icon: "event", on_click: ->(_event) { page.update(sort, value: "Sorted by date") }),

control-segment.summary: One option of a [`segmented_button`](/docs/control-segmented-button). `value` is required, and is what the button reports in `selected` and `on_change`; `label` and `icon` are what the user sees.
example: segment("grid", label: "Grid", icon: icon("grid_view"), tooltip: "Show a grid"),
segment("map", label: "Map", icon: icon("map"), disabled: true)

control-step.summary: One step of a [`stepper`](/docs/control-stepper), built with `stepper_step` (there is no bare `step` helper). `title` is required; `subtitle` and `label` add text, `content` is shown while the step is open, `state` picks its icon and `is_active` draws it in the active color. The stepper's handlers decide which step is open.
example: stepper_step(title: "Cart", subtitle: "2 items", state: "complete", is_active: true, content: text("Socks, Hat")),
stepper_step(title: "Shipping", state: "editing", is_active: true, content: text_field(label: "Address")),

control-submenu-button.summary: A button in a [`menu_bar`](/docs/control-menu-bar), or inside another submenu, that opens a menu of `controls`: [`menu_item_button`](/docs/control-menu-item-button)s, nested `submenu_button`s and `divider`s. `content` is its label. On Android, web, Windows and Linux the menu drops down under the button (or opens beside it when nested); on iOS and macOS it opens as a sheet from the bottom of the screen. `on_open` and `on_close` fire as it opens and closes.
example: menu_item_button("Upper case", on_click: ->(_event) { page.update(status, value: "UPPER CASE") }),
menu_item_button("Lower case", on_click: ->(_event) { page.update(status, value: "lower case") })

control-tab.summary: One tab of a [`tab_bar`](/docs/control-tab-bar), inside [`tabs`](/docs/control-tabs). `label` (the first positional argument) is a string or a control, and `icon` shows with it: above it on Android, web, Windows and Linux, before it on iOS and macOS. The tab has no events; the `tabs` control reports the selected index in `on_change`.
example: tab_bar_view([text("No recent calls"), text("No messages")], expand: true)

control-tab-bar.summary: The row of [`tab`](/docs/control-tab)s inside [`tabs`](/docs/control-tabs); it must be inside a `tabs` control, which holds the selection. On Android, web, Windows and Linux it is a Material tab bar with an indicator line under the selected tab, scrollable unless `scrollable: false`; on iOS and macOS it is a sliding segmented control whose thumb uses `indicator_color`, and the other styling keywords do not apply. `on_click` gets the tapped tab's index in `event.data`.
example: tab_bar_view([text("Today"), text("This week"), text("This month")], expand: true)

control-tab-bar-view.summary: The pages of [`tabs`](/docs/control-tabs), one per [`tab`](/docs/control-tab) and in the same order; it must be inside a `tabs` control. On Android, web, Windows and Linux the user can also swipe between pages; on iOS and macOS it shows the selected page only. Give it a height or `expand: true`: it shows an error when its height is unbounded.
example: column(children: [text("16 GB memory"), text("1 TB storage")])
